1  ORDER

The petitioner is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.PC in Crime No.307/2022 of Kudur Police Station, pending in S.C.No.111/2023 on the file of the learned III Additional District and Sessions Judge at Ramanagara, registered for the offences punishable under Section 376 of IPC on the basis of the first information lodged by Smt. Kamalamma.

entities.text: III Additional District and Sessions Judge at Ramanagara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Smt. Chaitra K.R., learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. Waheeda M.M., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the sole accused.
He is innocent and has not committed any offences as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
He was apprehended on 05.07.2022.
Since then, he is in judicial custody.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed.
Under such circumstances, detention of the petitioner would amount to pre trial punishment.
There are serious NC: 2024:KHC:6593 contradictions in the statements of the witnesses.
He is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause title to the petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, learned HCGP opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence.
CW-2 is the victim who is a deaf and dumb lady.
She is already married having two kids.
Her statement was recorded with the help of Special Educator in recording the statement.
The medical records support the contention of the prosecution.
The circumstantial witnesses have also stated in their statement regarding commission of the offence.
Under such circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.

Accordingly,
she prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is "Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.PC?"
NC: 2024:KHC:6593

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 6.
The petitioner was apprehended on 05.07.2022 on the basis of the FIR lodged by the informant alleging commission of the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.
The victim is cited as CW-2 in the charge sheet.
She is said to be a deaf and dumb lady.
She is married having two kids.
The prosecution is placing reliance on the first information lodged by the informant.
Statement of the victim is recorded with the help of the Special Educator.
There are also the circumstantial witnesses.
The medical report supports the contention of the prosecution.

CWs.1 to 6 are said to be the Gangadharaiah vs State Of Karnataka on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101687776/
2 material witnesses.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, definitely that will terrorize the victim and other witnesses.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail at this stage.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the 'Negative' and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
However, liberty is reserved in favour of the petitioner to move the trial Court with similar petition seeking grant of bail after examination of the material witnesses.
